item.title: Marines Field Next-Gen Tech to Survive the Post-Golden Hour Battlefield
item.dc:creator: Amarjeet Singh
item.description:
The 'golden hour' of battlefield medicine is dead. Facing near-peer adversaries in the Pacific, the Marine Corps is fielding self-contained blood banks and ultrasounds to keep casualties alive during extended evacuation delays.
[SPLIT] ⚡ The Marine Corps has deployed the Expeditionary Medical Refrigeration Unit (EMRU) and MEQU mobile blood warmers to maintain forward cold-chain distribution without heavy generators. [SPLIT] ⚡ Point-of-care ultrasound systems like the KOSMOS are being integrated to rapidly detect internal bleeding on the battlefield. item.title: The Real Mission of the Army's New Drone Techs Is Constant Adaptation
item.dc:creator: Amarjeet Singh
item.description:
Forget the joystick jockey in a bunker. The U.S. Army's new 390A warrant officers aren't drone pilots—they're frontline software engineers and tactical innovators built for the electronic warfare age.
[SPLIT] ⚡ Training protocols are heavily informed by empirical lessons from drone-heavy conflicts in Ukraine, Nagorno-Karabakh, and the Middle East. [SPLIT] ⚡ Curriculum architecture is intentionally designed to 'drive failure,' forcing candidates to innovate under severe electronic jamming and disconnected conditions.
